sections.name: Hell knight
sections.card:
Summary: 500 hit points make the Hell knight a serious fight. Up close it scratches; at range it throws green fireballs. The Doom 64 variant is less pale than the standard one and looks more like Doom's baron of Hell.
Weak points: Do not melee it: it scratches back, and the chainsaw is ineffective against a monster like this. Shoot it instead: its low pain chance means the rocket launcher, plasma gun or super shotgun are the most effective, with the chaingun and shotgun good at close range.
Tips: Keep your distance and its fireballs can be dodged, but do not underestimate them: they move quicker than imp or cacodemon fireballs and hit hard. In Doom 64 a Hell knight's fireballs hurt barons of Hell and theirs hurt it, so the two can be set against each other.

sections.name: Baron of Hell
sections.card:
Summary: Only the cyberdemon and the spiderdemon outlast it: a baron of Hell has 1000 hit points. It scratches when you are near and fires projectiles from afar. In Doom 64 the baron is red-orange and fires red projectiles, while green now belongs to the Hell knight.
Weak points: Distance and weapon choice decide this fight. Up close, stay out of melee, because its claws are a real hazard. Use the rocket launcher, plasma gun or super shotgun, which suit a monster that rarely flinches and soaks up punishment; the chaingun and shotgun are slow and only work if you can keep far enough away.
Tips: Where you fight matters: in a cramped space its fireballs become much deadlier, but in the open you can circle-strafe around most of them. Doom 64 adds a twist: barons and Hell knights can injure each other and end up infighting.

sections.name: Mancubus
sections.card:
Summary: Huge flamethrowers replace its arms, and it fires fireballs in bursts. The Doom 64 mancubus stands noticeably taller, with a metal harness and a fuel pack strapped on its back, and its fireballs are smaller and look like fiery brimstone. You first meet it in MAP09: Even Simpler.
Weak points: Its slowness and size make it an easy mark for rapid-fire weapons, and the rocket launcher may be the best choice. Before it fires it pauses and bellows a distinctive battle cry, which gives you time to stun it with a slower weapon, even the super shotgun, and stop the attack.
Tips: Back off while it attacks, since close up two fireballs can hit you instead of one. An unhurt mancubus finishes all three bursts even if you duck out of sight, which you can exploit to start monster infighting. In Doom 64 the fireballs fly off in a somewhat different direction than in Doom II.

sections.name: Arachnotron
sections.card:
Summary: A brain with two small arms sits in a large metal spider chassis. In Doom 64 it carries two guns that put out two blue plasma bolts at once, in spurts of five, and it keeps up the fire as long as you are in view. Its first appearance is MAP14: Eye of the Storm, unless you visit the secret levels MAP30: The Lair and MAP32: Hectic earlier, which hold some.
Weak points: A medium pain chance means fast-firing guns such as the chaingun work well on it. Skip the chainsaw: the arachnotron's size keeps the saw from reliably connecting.
Tips: Health vanishes quickly in its fire: the bolts travel faster than almost any other projectile, and it shoots them so often. Beat it by never stopping: keep attacking, sweep side to side in wide moves, and duck out of its line of fire now and then, and you take minimal damage. When monsters fight each other in Doom 64, its twin plasma cannons often beat even a baron of Hell, leaving little health.

sections.name: Cacodemon
sections.card:
Summary: A cacodemon floats slowly, grins with a wide mouth, and either spits a ball of lightning or bites. In Doom 64 it is beige brown, with just one eye, yellow-green, and two arms ending in broken chains; the arms swing as it flies.
Weak points: Hits knock it back easily and it moves slowly, which makes it one of the easier targets. Use a chaingun or plasma gun to keep it pushed away so it barely fights back, or the chainsaw to incapacitate it.
Tips: Doom 64 keeps the faster cacodemon shots of the PlayStation version, but the cacodemons themselves are as slow as in DOS. With room to move you can fight many at once and take little or no damage, as the shots are easy to dodge. Watch for ones flying out of unexpected places once alerted.

sections.name: Pain elemental
sections.card:
Summary: This floating monster shoots no projectile; it lets lost souls fly at you every so often. The Doom 64 version is dark pink with a green eye, and two mouths where its arms were, letting it spawn two lost souls at once. When it spots you it laughs, low and sinister.
Weak points: Kill order matters: the pain elemental first, its lost souls only afterward. Weapon choice matters too: the chaingun and plasma gun fire fast enough to usually keep lost souls at bay, whereas the rocket launcher is risky because a lost soul can be spat out while your rocket is still flying, and the blast can reach you.
Tips: Unlike other versions, standing right against it does not stop the lost souls: in Doom 64 every one that cannot materialize, including those released when it dies, explodes like a barrel, and getting hit by two is about as bad as a rocket. It spawns lost souls only while something that attacked it can see it, so hit it hard, then break line of sight.

sections.name: Cyberdemon
sections.card:
Summary: Its left arm is a big rocket launcher, and it has 4000 hit points. In Doom 64 its skin is darker and it is far larger than the PC version, and its rockets trail smoke. Cyberdemons are uncommon: you meet them mostly in the secret levels or late in the game.
Weak points: Use the BFG9000 if you have it; the plasma gun is a fairly good second choice. Without a BFG the rocket launcher is also effective, though the fight drags on, and every rocket must score a direct hit because blast damage does nothing to it. Other weapons are much harder, and melee is extremely hard, so avoid them.
Tips: You cannot easily stagger it out of attacking: its pain chance is low. Circle-strafe, and treat every rocket as dangerous, because a single one can critically injure you. The Doom 64 version fires faster rockets (700 to 900 units per second) from the launcher itself, so they head down toward you and explode on the floor near you even when no wall is close. On Watch Me Die, MAP17: Watch Your Step ends with two cyberdemons and MAP24: No Escape has three.

sections.name: Lost soul
sections.card:
Summary: The lost soul is a weapon itself, charging with its jaws open. Doom 64's version has black horns and an opened skull with fire only on top; it has less health but is much more aggressive, and recovers much faster after each attack. That viciousness makes it among the deadliest enemies.
Weak points: Fire at a charging lost soul and the charge stops; it is then helpless until it hits something, which is why the chaingun suits a crowd. It is also weaker than on PC: one shotgun blast fells it.
Tips: Rockets are risky in a group, as a lost soul may dart toward you and make a rocket explode near enough to hurt you. Watch for the warning signs: unlike every other monster it makes no sound when alerted, so the hissing breath of its launch is often the first clue. Expect groups more often than singles.

sections.name: Demon and spectre
sections.card:
Summary: Demons and spectres attack only in melee, and quickly. Doom 64's manual calls the demon the bull demon, and it looks more menacing: black horns, smaller red eyes, bigger teeth and claws, plus a bit more melee reach. A Doom 64 spectre starts out looking like a green-tinted, opaque demon and becomes translucent once it detects you.
Weak points: Stay at range and they cannot hurt you, since they have no ranged attack. When one gets close, a super shotgun blast kills it outright, the chaingun does well too, and you can hit and run with the shotgun. The chainsaw keeps a demon from attacking while it cuts, and costs no ammo.
Tips: Their fast zig-zag runs close the gap quickly and can pin you in a corner. Lead them into a tight corridor with the chainsaw so they cannot surround you. Of the monsters, they are the easiest to draw into attacking each other.

sections.name: Chainsaw
sections.card:
Summary: The chainsaw shreds enemies near enough to touch, acting roughly like a fist that hits four times as fast, and it uses no ammo. The Doom 64 saw has two blades rather than one, the letters "U.A.C." engraved on top, and about double the damage of the PC saw.
Uses: Demons and spectres are its best targets, since you can usually kill them without being hurt. It also does fairly well on cacodemons and imps. Anything that flinches easily is a good target too, because the saw holds them back. Against enemies that hit hard and rarely flinch, such as Hell knights, it does not work.
Tips: With a reach of only 65 map units against the fist's 64, you must be almost on top of the target. A pack of demons is best handled by backing into a corner and sawing them down one at a time. In the open with several enemies, a berserk fist kills faster, so the saw becomes a liability.

sections.name: BFG9000
sections.card:
Summary: This is Doom's ultimate weapon: it fires large green plasma spheres. A single shot can destroy almost any monster, and the damage spreads over a wide area, so several targets can be hit at once. The Doom 64 BFG has a darker color scheme and first turns up in MAP10: The Bleeding.
Uses: The damage spreads over a wide area, which suits groups. The plasma ball explodes when it hits something solid, and 40 invisible tracer rays then go out from you in a cone in the direction the ball flew. Even cyberdemons and spiderdemons, which blast damage cannot hurt, are hit by those rays.
Tips: It does not fire the instant you pull the trigger: in Doom 64 there is a wait of exactly one second before the ball leaves, and the rays follow about half a second after it hits. The rays go in the direction the ball was fired even if you turn, so keep facing your target. A shot takes 40 cells, and a BFG you pick up holds 40.

sections.name: Megasphere
sections.card:
Summary: A gray-brown orb that sets both your health and your armour to 200 percent; the armour is the same as blue armour. In Doom 64 it shows a helmet like the player's instead of a demonic face.
Uses: One pickup tops up both health and armour at once. It also counts toward the items percentage on the end-of-level screen.
Tips: The first one in Doom 64 is in MAP06: Alpha Quadrant, and the game holds nine or ten of them, depending on the skill level.

sections.name: Super shotgun
sections.card:
Summary: A sawed-off, break-open double-barrel shotgun. Each shot spends two shells and sends out 20 pellets (the normal shotgun sends seven), so per shot it hits for roughly triple what a standard shotgun does. In Doom 64 it reloads faster: 1.53 seconds against 1.77 in Doom II. It also knocks you back slightly, and it ranks among the most essential weapons in that game.
Uses: Line up a shot and one blast will almost always finish two imps, or one demon or spectre. It also helps you hold your own against crowds of humanoids and tough monsters (Hell knights, arachnotrons, mancubi). Against those monsters it is often wiser than the rocket launcher: similar power, shells are easier to come by than rockets, and a rocket exploding up close can hurt you.
Tips: The pellets spread wide, even up and down, so it is wasteful at long range: switch to the shotgun to snipe, or to deal with a lone enemy in a maze. It uses the same shells as the shotgun.

sections.name: Plasma gun
sections.card:
Summary: A rapid-fire gun that fires bursts of blue plasma and draws on the same energy cells as the BFG9000. The Doom 64 version has a blue electric tube on its top that buzzes without stopping.
Uses: It is devastating against almost any single opponent and works as the game's all-rounder. Firing continuously halts an arachnotron or a mancubus in its tracks and cuts a baron of Hell's speed and attack rate roughly in half.
Tips: In Doom 64 it fires a little slower than on PC, one shot every 0.133 seconds, but there is no pause after you let go of the trigger and the shots travel faster. At long range, targets usually move too much for a stream of shots to land, so fire short controlled bursts instead of holding the trigger down.

sections.name: Berserk pack
sections.card:
Summary: Looks like a dark gray medikit. Picking it up makes your fists hit far harder and tops your health up to 100 percent, unless you already have 100 or more. A red haze fills the screen for a while; in Doom 64 it lasts only three seconds.
Uses: It makes your punch ten times stronger, usually until the level ends or you die: strong enough to turn humanoids to pulp, and sometimes to kill a demon in a single blow. Picking it up switches your current weapon to the fist, so you can suddenly find yourself unarmed.
Tips: The extra strength does not run out when the red haze fades, so do not stop punching because the screen has cleared. Use it hit-and-run: run up, punch, then retreat or dodge. A punch does not latch on like the chainsaw, so aim carefully.
